rv.q: London’s tiny Theatre comes into its own for this UK premiere of Simon Stephens’ meditative and bleakly funny post-apocalyptic new play.
It's not yet a magnum opus but a climate drama that, with some tweaks, holds great potential.

The production, which premiered at Glass Mask theatre in Dublin earlier this year and is again directed by Rex Ryan, is in no rush to reveal its world and the games played within it, making you work to imagine your own apocalypse outside.
But there is also a sense of archness and artificiality to the dialogue and the plot, such as it is – of random elements thrown in to trip the audience up again.
A tense three‑hander set in a claustrophobic bunker and driven by strong performances, striking design and clever storytelling.
The company is charming and the characters most definitely grow on you, but it's rather indecisive and inconclusive in its aims.

cn.t: Stephens' claustrophobic bunker drama earns praise for strong performances and striking design, but critics split on execution—some find it tense and timely, others deem it bland and light on tension.
